body: We want to  move `allocationService.reroute(newState, "state recovered")` to callback method  `RecoverStateUpdateTask#clusterStateProcessed`,and in it we can  submit a `ClusterStateUpdateTask` that execute `allocationService.reroute(currentState, "state recovered")`

I'm not sure I understand the impact of this: the task in question doesn't change any cluster settings so the latest persistent settings should all be applied already. Could you share some more details of which settings this affects and what the unexpected behaviour is? Maybe open a PR with a test that shows the problem?
I'm closing this due to the lack of response, but we're happy to reopen it if we receive more details about how this is a problem.

Sorry, I missed this reply. I'm trying [#81081](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/81081/files). I setted up `cluster.routing.allocation.batch_fetch_shard.enable` is true  in persistent settings, and full restart the whole cluster. And I found that the logic of single fetch was executed  which should execute batch fetch logic.
I Jstack the process,  and found that the RecoverStateUpdateTask executed first after full restart, and at the time ,the persistent settings was not updating by master.

Ok I see. The reason we don't see the persistent settings in this first reroute is that they're not applied while the `STATE_NOT_RECOVERED_BLOCK` is in place, because of this check for `disableStatePersistence()`:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/12ad399c488f0cc60e19b5e1b29c6d569cb4351a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/service/ClusterApplierService.java#L494-L500

In the specific case of `cluster.routing.allocation.batch_fetch_shard.enable` I think this setting should not be dynamic anyway (and possibly even not a setting) but more generally I see how this could be problem.

Thank you so much, I temporarily solved this problem by add the settings to `elasticsearch.yml`, but I think this way contains potential risks, there is always the possibility that someone forgets to add a setting similar to `cluster.routing.allocation.batch_fetch_shard.enable` to the `elasticsearch.yml` file.

issue.title: Reroute after cluster recovery

labels.name: :Distributed/Allocation
labels.description: All issues relating to the decision making around placing a shard (both master logic & on the nodes)

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Today when starting the cluster we open the routing table and reroute in
a single cluster state update, which means that this reroute runs before
any cluster settings have been applied. This doesn't make much
difference today since the initial reroute just triggers async shard
fetching so there are no settings which affect it, but it's still
surprising and would result in a bug if such a setting were introduced.
With this commit we trigger the first reroute in a follow-up cluster
state update instead so that any persistent settings are sure to be
applied.

Closes #82456
